title: Register Follow Market strategies and restore Production log visibility
author: agent:/root

scope.goal: Correct only the two verified post-deploy defects: register the already implemented 270 BTC/ETH/SOL Follow Market strategies through the next ordered migration, and make the Production service write its current Serilog files to the server log directory exposed for monitoring.
inScope: Add ordered transactional migration 0005 that inserts exactly the 270 existing Follow Market catalog rows: 90 each for BTC, ETH, and SOL; M=30..270 step 30; N=50..95 step 5.
Seed each exact catalog UUID, code, name, and description as enabled Paper configuration with live_stakes=false and no manual/automatic pause.
Make migration 0005 idempotent and checksum-bound without changing migrations 0001 through 0004 or immutable baseline SQL.
Configure Production file logging to server-local D:\1\logs while preserving AppContext.BaseDirectory\logs as the default outside Production.

If the configured Production directory cannot be created before Serilog initialization, emit an explicit console diagnostic and fall back to AppContext.BaseDirectory\logs so logging-path failure does not prevent service startup.
Add focused migration, catalog parity, configuration/path-resolution, and file-write tests; build and independently review the exact diff.
outOfScope: Changing Follow Market decision, threshold, direction, FAK, sizing, fill, retry, PaperOnly, settlement, fee, or risk behavior already approved under RC-20260829-follow-market-fak-strategies.
Any strategy other than the exact existing 270 Follow Market variants; any historical backfill or recalculation.
Enabling Live stakes, placing/cancelling an order, deploying, restarting/stopping the service, changing Production database state manually, or changing the Windows share/configuration remotely.
Changing migrations 0001 through 0004, their SQL/checksums/order, or adding any schema object unrelated to the exact strategy registration.
Logging framework replacement, retention-policy changes, remote log shipping, database logging, telemetry expansion, or unrelated startup/refactoring work.
scope.periodOrFilter: Exact existing 270 Follow Market variants and service file logging for future starts after the user's later deployment; no historical period and no current Production mutation.
scope.firstVerification: Inspect the exact catalog identifiers, strategies table defaults and ordered migration path; inspect the current Serilog initialization, Production configuration loading, output-copy behavior, and focused test seams before product edits.

requirements.text: Register exactly the already approved 270 Follow Market variants in PostgreSQL through ordered migration 0005 so runtime settings no longer disable them because their strategy rows are missing.
acceptanceCriteria: Migration 0005 contains exactly 270 unique UUID/code pairs matching the deployed StrategyIds Follow Market catalog: 90 per BTC/ETH/SOL and the exact M/N cross product.
Every seeded row is enabled=true, live_stakes=false, paused=false, auto_live_paused=false, paper_stake_amount=1.00, live_stake_amount=1.00, and live_available_balance=100.00 on initial insert.

On ID conflict with the same exact code, the migration refreshes catalog name/description, enables Paper, disables Live and clears pause state without deleting history; any ID/code or code/ID collision fails the transaction rather than overwriting another strategy.
Migration 0005 is transactional, has one fixed semantic checksum, is ordered after 0004, records one ledger row, and a second initializer run is metadata-only/idempotent.
Immutable baseline 0001 and ordered migrations 0002, 0003, and 0004 remain unchanged.
A disposable local PostgreSQL integration test proves zero-to-270 insertion, exact catalog parity, Live-disabled state, collision failure, singleton ledger registration, and idempotent second run.

verification.command: Run focused PostgresSchemaMigrationTests against an allowlisted disposable local PostgreSQL database with all outputs under the marked D:\CodexTemp run.
verification.expected: Exactly 270 catalog-matching Follow Market rows are inserted with the approved runtime flags; collisions fail closed; migration ledger and rerun are idempotent; migrations 0001..0004 are unchanged.
verification.evidence: The final focused checksum/catalog suite passed 7/7 together with the logging tests. The real PostgreSQL regression passed 3/3 against the exact disposable local database pct_codex_follow_market_regression3_20260829_c00fce4d: full baseline plus migration 0005, exact 270-row catalog parity and flags, singleton ledger/idempotent rerun, and both ID/code collision rollbacks. Individual durations were 1.317s, 0.423s, and 0.967s, confirming the database branches executed. The disposable database was dropped and verified absent (remaining count 0).

requirements.text: Make Production service logs visible again in the authorized server log location without making an unavailable configured directory fatal to service startup.
acceptanceCriteria: Production configuration resolves the primary file-log directory to exactly D:\1\logs; non-Production/default configuration remains AppContext.BaseDirectory\logs.
The resolver accepts an explicit ServiceLogging:Directory override, canonicalizes it to an absolute path, and rejects an empty/invalid path with an explicit diagnostic.

Before constructing the Serilog file sink, the service creates the resolved directory. If creation fails, it writes the exact failure and fallback path to stderr and initializes Serilog under AppContext.BaseDirectory\logs instead of terminating solely because the configured log path failed.
The service logs the selected absolute file directory at startup without exposing credentials or other secrets.

A focused test with disposable directories proves Production resolution, default resolution, successful file creation/write/flush, and the nonfatal fallback path; publish/build evidence confirms appsettings.Production.json is included in the service output.

verification.command: Run focused ServiceLogPathResolver and Serilog file-sink tests with all directories and results under the marked D:\CodexTemp run.
verification.expected: Production selects D:\1\logs, other environments retain the executable-local default, a writable configured directory receives a flushed log record, and an unavailable directory falls back with an explicit diagnostic without aborting logger creation.
verification.evidence: Final ServiceLogPathResolverTests passed 5/5, including configured/default resolution, explicit empty override diagnostic and fallback, unavailable-directory IOException diagnostic and fallback, and an actual flushed Serilog file record. The combined final resolver plus migration-checksum suite passed 7/7 with zero failures or skips.

verification.command: Build and publish PolyCopyTrader.Service plus build PolyCopyTrader.sln in Release with disposable outputs under the marked D:\CodexTemp run; inspect publish configuration files.
verification.expected: Build/publish complete with zero errors and appsettings.Production.json containing D:\1\logs is present in publish output.
verification.evidence: Final Release solution build completed with 0 warnings and 0 errors. Final PolyCopyTrader.Service Release publish succeeded; the exact published appsettings.Production.json was present and resolved ServiceLogging.Directory to D:\1\logs, and PolyCopyTrader.Service.exe was present.

assumptions.text: The authorized SMB share \\192.168.0.101\CodexLogs exposes the server-local directory D:\1\logs previously identified by the user.
assumptions.impact: After the user deploys and restarts the service, directing the Production file sink to D:\1\logs should make new files visible through CodexLogs. If the share maps another physical directory, source behavior will be correct for D:\1\logs but the share itself will still require a separate server-side correction.
